channel.title: Polymath — Knowledge, beautifully organized.
channel.description: Polymath is a free, open knowledge hub exploring AI, machine learning, data science, mathematics, physics, cryptography, finance, history, science and technology — with a community that discusses, questions and learns together.

item.title: Why LLMs Hallucinate (and How to Keep Them Honest)
item.description: Large language models sometimes state false things with total confidence. Understanding why reveals how to use them safely — and where they genuinely shine.

item.title: Decision Trees and Random Forests, Explained Simply
item.description: One of the most intuitive ideas in machine learning — asking a series of yes/no questions — scales into one of the most reliable. Here's how, and why a 'forest' beats a single tree.

item.title: Attention, Explained: How Transformers Actually Think
item.description: The self-attention mechanism powers nearly every modern AI model. Here's an intuitive, jargon-light walkthrough of what it does and why it changed everything.

item.title: Correlation Is Not Causation: The Most Important Stats Lesson
item.description: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together — but ice cream isn't the killer. A practical guide to the trap that fools experts, headlines, and algorithms alike.

item.title: The Bias–Variance Tradeoff, Without the Hand-Waving
item.description: Why your model can be wrong in two completely different ways — and how understanding the tension between them makes you a better practitioner.

item.title: The Monty Hall Problem: When Intuition Goes to War with Math
item.description: Three doors, one car, two goats. A puzzle so counterintuitive it fooled mathematicians — and a perfect lesson in how new information changes probability.

item.title: Data Cleaning: The Unglamorous 80% of Data Science
item.description: Models get the glory, but data preparation decides whether a project succeeds. A field guide to the messy, essential work nobody puts in their portfolio.

item.title: Special Relativity: Why Time Is Not the Same for Everyone
item.description: Move fast enough and your clock genuinely runs slow compared to someone standing still. It sounds like science fiction — but GPS satellites correct for it every day.

item.title: Why the Number e Shows Up Everywhere
item.description: Compound interest, population growth, radioactive decay, and probability all lead to the same constant: 2.71828… Here's the single idea that ties them together.

item.title: Hash Functions: The Internet's Fingerprints
item.description: They verify your downloads, store your passwords, and hold blockchains together. A clear look at what cryptographic hash functions do and why they're irreversible.

item.title: Quantum Entanglement Without the Mysticism
item.description: It's been called 'spooky action at a distance,' but entanglement doesn't let you send signals faster than light. Here's what it really is — and isn't.

item.title: Diversification: The Only Free Lunch in Investing
item.description: There's a way to reduce risk without reducing expected return. It's not magic — it's math — and it's the single most reliable idea in finance.

item.title: How RSA Lets Strangers Share Secrets
item.description: Every time you see a padlock in your browser, public-key cryptography is at work. Here's the elegant number theory that lets two people who've never met communicate securely.

item.title: Compound Interest: The Most Powerful Force You're Ignoring
item.description: Time, not timing, builds wealth. A clear-eyed look at how compounding works, why starting early beats investing more, and the traps that quietly eat your returns.

item.title: Entropy and the Arrow of Time
item.description: Why can you unscramble an egg in a video played backward, but never in real life? The answer — entropy — may be the deepest reason time only flows one way.

item.title: CRISPR: How We Learned to Edit Life Itself
item.description: A bacterial immune system became the most powerful gene-editing tool ever invented. Here's how CRISPR works, what it can already do, and the questions it forces us to ask.

item.title: P vs NP: Computer Science's Million-Dollar Question
item.description: Is finding a solution as easy as checking one? It sounds simple, but the answer would reshape cryptography, science, and our understanding of creativity itself.

item.title: What Actually Happens When You Open a Website
item.description: You type a URL and a page appears. Between those two moments, a remarkable global relay race takes place in milliseconds. Here's the whole journey.

item.title: Zero: The Most Important Number That Almost Wasn't
item.description: Civilizations built pyramids and predicted eclipses without it. The story of how humanity invented 'nothing' is a journey through India, the Islamic world, and centuries of resistance.

item.title: The Printing Press and the Original Information Revolution
item.description: Five centuries before the internet, one machine shattered the monopoly on knowledge and reshaped religion, science, and politics. The parallels to our own moment are striking.

item.title: Algorithmic Bias: How Neutral-Looking Models Learn Unfairness
item.description: An algorithm has no opinions — so how does it end up discriminating? Understanding where bias enters is the first step to building AI that's actually fair.

item.title: Gradient Descent: How Machines Learn by Walking Downhill
item.description: Nearly every model you've heard of is trained by the same simple idea — feel which way is downhill, take a step, repeat. Here's the intuition behind the workhorse of machine learning.

item.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Math of Changing Your Mind
item.description: A single formula tells you how much to update a belief when new evidence arrives. It's the backbone of spam filters, medical tests, and clear thinking itself.
